Render a document to HTML

Source: R/render_html.R
pub_html.Rd

Renders a document (see pub_doc()) to an HTML fragment, which can be used in Shiny UIs directly. pub_render() writes a standalone HTML file instead.

Usage

pub_html(
  doc,
  cache = NULL,
  toc = TRUE,
  math = c("mathjax", "none"),
  figure = list(device = "png", res = 200)
)

Arguments

doc

A pub_doc.

cache

A pub_cache() or NULL (render every figure and table).

toc

TRUE: add a table of contents (headings up to level 3).

math

"mathjax": attach MathJax if the document has math; "none": math stays as \(...\) and \[...\].

figure

Device settings of figures: device ("png" or "svg") and res (resolution of PNG images in dpi; 200 as in the viewer and every format of pub_render(), so they share the cached figures).

Value

HTML (an htmltools::HTML() string with dependencies).

Details

Contents

The result has:

  • a header with the title, subtitle and metadata;

  • an optional table of contents;

  • one <section> per section, with numbered headings.

Tables are rendered with huxtable (see pub_table()), figures as inline PNG (or SVG) images, text as Markdown (CommonMark), math with MathJax and error items (failed steps, see pub_doc()) as error boxes. Raw HTML in texts is shown as text; use pub_raw() to insert HTML.

Dependencies

The result carries its CSS (pubflow-doc.css) and, if the document has math, MathJax 3 (from a CDN) as HTML dependencies.

Caching

Rendering a figure takes about 0.1 s and the HTML of a table several milliseconds. With a cache, both are rendered once and reused while they are unchanged:

  • Use one cache per Shiny session (or R process) and pass it to the viewer and to every render call. They then share the figures (with the same device settings, a figure is rendered once).

  • Only figures made by pipeline steps are cached. pubflow stamps each figure that a step returns (also in plain lists) with the step, its partition key and the time of the run. So whenever the step runs again (e.g. because a step parameter changed), its figures are re-rendered.

  • Figures without a stamp are rendered every time. These can be figures made outside a pipeline or inside the step that builds the document (the layout step). To have a figure cached, create it in a pipeline step of its own and pass it to the layout step as an input (e.g. plot = ~plot_step).

  • Figures rendered in their step (pub_figure(render = TRUE)) are not cached: the document uses their png as it is.

Cross-references

Cross-references in texts (see pub_text()) link to their figure or table. A reference that can't be resolved is marked in the HTML and gives a pubflow_render_warning, so a draft still displays. On the other hand, pub_render() never allows undefined references and stops with an error instead.

See also

pub_render(), pub_cache(), pub_doc()

Examples

doc <- pub_doc(
    pub_section(
        "Results",
        pub_text("Mean ozone peaks in **August** ($x_8 = 60$ ppb)."),
        pub_table(aggregate(Ozone ~ Month, data = airquality, FUN = mean),
                  caption = "Mean ozone", digits = c(Ozone = 1L))
    ),
    title = "Demo"
)
html <- pub_html(doc)
cat(substr(html, 1, 300))
#> <div class="pubflow-doc">
#> <header class="pubflow-doc-header">
#> <h1 class="pubflow-title">Demo</h1>
#> </header>
#> <nav class="pubflow-toc">
#> <ul>
#> <li><a href="#pubflow-sec-1"><span class="pubflow-section-number">1</span> Results</a>
#> </li>
#> </ul>
#> </nav>
#> <section class="pubflow-section pubflow-level-1" id="pu
